Communication, in detail

The comm graph, the gossip channel, the shared belief, the learned fusion, and the connectivity metric — exactly as the code does it, with the graph shown live.

Comms is the bridge of the formalism: the time-varying graph that turns a set of agents into a team. Every agent acts on its own local view plus whatever its neighbours tell it. This page traces that path end to end — what the graph is, what rides it, how beliefs fuse, and how connectivity is measured and constrained.

1 · The comm graph

Two agents share an edge iff they are within Chebyshev distance comm_r (an L∞ square, radius 5 by default). The graph is symmetric and every agent has a self-loop (it always hears itself, which keeps the gossip belief monotone). There are two layers: the potential graph (who could talk, derived from positions) and the delivered graph (what the channel actually carried). The reward and all connectivity metrics read the potential graph recomputed from positions, not the delivered one.

thingdefinitionwhere
DiskTopologyadjacency = max|posᵢ−posⱼ| ≤ comm_r, symmetric, diagonal True (Chebyshev only)comms.py:49-71

2 · Wall-RF occlusion — an option, off by default

Walls can be made to degrade links: the effective distance inflates to d_eff = d + c·k, where c = comm_r/3 ≈ 1.67 and k = the number of separate wall-runs the straight segment crosses (a thick wall counts once). The graph then thresholds d_eff ≤ comm_r, so a marginal through-wall link drops.

Honest note: occlusion is OFF by default and was off in these runs (world.occlusion=False), so d_eff = d and comms pass straight through walls here. Even when enabled, occlusion only affects the CTDE-side metric/GNN graph (kb_adjacency, λ₂) — the gossip channel still delivers over the plain through-wall disk. So belief can flood past a wall that the connectivity metric penalizes. env_utils.py:166-194 · config.py:75

3 · The channel and what rides it

The channel is a delayed, lossy gossip flood (GossipChannel) over the disk. In these runs it runs at recipe defaults: delay = 1 step, dropout = 0 (lossless), bandwidth = none. Each tick every agent broadcasts its one-step-old belief to in-range neighbours, who OR it into their own — single-hop per tick, but multi-hop across successive steps because everyone re-broadcasts every step.

What rides the channel is not positions, not roles, not trust — it is a single OR-reducible boolean grid: each agent's known-cells belief (its own coverage trail unioned with the walls/occupancy it has sensed). One payload type, by deliberate design.

parametervalue (these runs)note

dropout (channel)0.0no packet loss. (config.dropout is a neural-net dropout — a different thing) comms.py:145-158
bandwidthNoneunbounded; the bool payload has no step-stamps to rank by comms.py:110-116

4 · Sensing and the shared belief

Each agent directly senses a Chebyshev disk of radius sense_r = 1 — just its 3×3 ring. With sense_walls on it folds the walls it sees into its belief; with sense_free on (these runs) it stores the whole sensed disk as a free/occupied map. The belief is monotone — a union that never forgets, SLAM-style — and it is the only map the policy reads (world.channel.shared); ground truth is reserved for the central critic. This is the right panel of the demo above filling in.

Because sense_r=1, an agent knows almost nothing on its own — its map is mostly what neighbours gossiped. So connectivity directly feeds the belief, and early in an episode (near-empty belief) the team is effectively near-blind. That is why the belief starts at ~1–2% and climbs. env.py:301-321 · obs.py:64-80 · ppo.py:109-122

5 · The learned fusion (GNN-KB)

On the actor side, the belief is fused across the comm graph by an LPAC-style backbone: each agent runs a CNN, global-average-pools to a feature, then does 2 rounds of message-passing (MPLayer) over kb_adjacency, producing a per-agent embedding every head reads. Two rounds = a 2-hop receptive field. The aggregator is max by default (also mean or softmax-attention), all normalized — never a raw sum — which is what makes the same weights work at any team size or grid size. By default the message is a pure learned transform of the belief; an optional channel appends the comm_r-normalized edge distance (scale-invariant geometry).

rounds (mp_rounds)2 → 2-hop fusion (LPAC, Gama et al. 2024) nets.py:315-339 · config.py:125
aggregatormax (default) · mean (degree-normalized) · multihead (softmax) — all count-independent nets.py:210-233
message contentlearned transform of belief (default); optional edge_distance = kb_distance/comm_r ∈ [0,1] nets.py:130-149
trust weightingnone — every in-range message fused equally (trust-by-default, no anomaly gate) nets.py:208-233

6 · Connectivity — measured & constrained

Connectivity is a single scalar: build a soft comm graph with weights w = σ(2·(comm_r − d)), take the Fiedler value λ₂ (second-smallest Laplacian eigenvalue) of its Laplacian. λ₂ > 0 ⟺ connected; larger = more robustly linked. That's the number in the demo's left panel.

Two grading bars read the same λ₂: connectivity_pct (λ₂ > 10⁻³, a trivial "connected at all" floor a huddle passes for free) and connectivity_real (λ₂ > 0.5, the honest bar). Both are diagnostic only — neither enters the loss. The constraint acts through the reward: a soft penalty (fixed, or a Lagrangian dual weight dual-ascended on the realized shortfall), fed by either a global λ₂-shortfall or a per-agent degree margin.

Two honest caveats. (1) The shipped default mechanism is action_mask — a hard mask that forbids disconnecting moves; the soft/Lagrangian options run only when explicitly selected, so which one a run used must be checked per-run (it matters: a hard mask makes connectivity unbreakable, which would defeat the resilience study). (2) The Lagrangian threshold defaults to 10⁻³, below the natural λ₂, so the dual rarely engages — connectivity is mostly shaped by a separate always-on reward term (reach_fraction, weight 2.0), not the guardrail. ppo.py:82-102,1235-1248 · config.py:260,319

7 · How it maps to the formalism

formalismcode
G_t = (I, E_t)kb_adjacency — time-varying in-range graph from positions
m_t^{j→i}MPLayer.msg — the learned per-agent message
c_t^i = Agg_i(·)the normalized (max/mean/attention) aggregate → belief z_i
trust-by-default (A6)no per-neighbour trust score / no Byzantine filter in v0

The bridge touches the mission twice: it shapes each agent's input (the GNN belief that drives the goal head) and it composes into the state (the soft λ₂ that feeds reward and safety). One caveat for the adversarial line: the code's E_t is undirected (symmetric), while the formalism allows a directed graph — an asymmetric or lying edge is exactly the attack surface a covert red agent would open, and it would have to be added on top of this symmetric substrate.
